drivers.name: AudioSynth
drivers.description: Software audio synthesizer. Plays tones, musical notes, and short melodies — useful for lab-side audible notifications, robot/CNC feedback tones, and experiment-complete bell sounds. Polyphonic via overlap: true so notes can ring into each other; long-tail presets (bell, marimba) decay naturally past the gate-on duration. Streams Opus-encoded audio to every connected dashboard by default; can also (or instead) play locally via NAudio on Windows hosts. Four waveforms, ADSR envelopes, additive harmonics, and presets (beep / bell / pluck / pad / marimba).
drivers.changelog:
## 1.5.0

### Features

- **Polyphony.** `playTone`, `playNote`, `playMelody`, and `beep` now accept
  `overlap: true`. The note is mixed on top of whatever voices are already
  ringing and the action returns at the gate-off so the next call can start
  before the tail finishes. The previous replace-not-queue behaviour is the
  default (`overlap: false`) — existing scripts and connectors continue to
  work unchanged.
- **Release tails ring out past gate-off.** Long-decay presets like `bell`
  and `marimba` are no longer compressed into the requested duration —
  a 200 ms bell now decays for its full ~1.5 s natural tail instead of
  being suddenly cut off. The action call still blocks until the tail
  finishes when `overlap` is `false`; `playing` reflects the full
  tail-out window.
- **Polyphonic NAudio output** runs through a single persistent
  `WaveOutEvent` driven by a sample-mixer, so overlapping voices on
  Windows host playback don't spawn an output device per note.
- **Polyphonic streaming output** uses the host's new live encoder
  session — one long-lived Opus encoder spans every overlapping voice
  and a 1 s post-silence linger window, so back-to-back overlap calls
  don't restart the encoder and glitch the browser-side decoder.

### Notes

- Requires the matching MuxitServer host change (adds
  `AudioStreamReaderEmitter` on `IConnectorDriver`). Older hosts will
  fall back to monophonic streaming when `overlap: true` is requested
  in browser mode — NAudio polyphony still works.

drivers.name: Lunatone DALI-2 USB (LUBA)
drivers.description: DALI-2 bus master via a Lunatone DALI-2 USB interface (LUBA protocol): levels, status, settings read/write, D4i memory banks, addressing.
drivers.changelog:
## 0.4.0

- **Every property and action is renamed, and names now start with the layer they talk to:** `usb…` for the Lunatone interface, `bus…` for the whole DALI line, `unit…` for one DALI address. **If you have scripts or dashboards for 0.3.x, rename the calls:** `open`/`release` → `usbOpen`/`usbRelease`, `interfaceInfo` → `usbInfo`, `busStatus` → `busRefresh` / `busScan`, `scan` → `busScan`, `assignAddresses` → `busAssignAddresses`, `sendRaw16` → `busSendRaw`, `setLevel` → `unitSetLevel`, `queryActualLevel` → `unitLevel`, `readStatus` → `unitStatus`, `readSettings` → `unitSettings`, `storeSettings` → `unitConfigure`, `setShortAddress` → `unitSetAddress`, `setDimmingCurve` → `unitSetCurve`, `identify` → `unitIdentify`, `reset` → `unitReset`, `readD4i` → `unitD4i`, `readMemoryBank` → `unitMemoryBank`, `query` → `unitQuery`; properties `connected` → `usbConnected`, `port` → `usbPort`.
- Removed as redundant: `off`, `recallMax`, `recallMin` (use `unitSetLevel`, 0 = off), `queryStatus` (part of `unitStatus`), `queryDimmingCurve` (part of `unitSettings`), `lineStatus` (the heartbeat keeps `busPowered` live), `writeMode` and `interfaceSettings` (now `usbInfo().settings`).
- **The USB link is watched: an unplugged interface now shows as disconnected.** Previously `connected` stayed `true` until `release`, because the serial port still reads as open after the device disappears. A heartbeat (READ STATUS every `heartbeatMs`, default 2000) checks that the interface answers. A failed write or two consecutive LUBA timeouts mark the link as lost. New: `usbState` (`ok`, `notFound`, `portBusy`, `noResponse`, `released`, `notConfigured`, `closed`, `error`), `usbMessage` and a live `busPowered`.
- Auto-reconnect: while the link is down the driver reopens the port every `reconnectMs` (default 3000), so plugging the interface back in recovers on its own. `usbRelease` stops this until `usbOpen`, so the MultiOne hand-over is not affected. A missing or busy interface at startup no longer stops the connector from loading.
- The dashboard values moved from the template into the driver: `status` (`OK`, `FAIL`, `NO UNITS`, `NO DATA`, `NO BUS`, `NO USB`, `PORT BUSY`, `NO RESPONSE`, `RELEASED`, `NO PORT`, `OFFLINE`), `statusText` (now with the failures), `lastUpdate`, `units` (now the unit list, `level` instead of `actualLevel`), `unitCount`, `unitLevels` and the writable broadcast level `busLevel`. The `dali` template is now only config and AI instructions; its short-name methods are gone because driver actions take positional arguments directly.
- `unitConfigure(3, {maxLevel: 200})` works from a script. The old `storeSettings(3, {…})` silently wrote nothing, because the trailing object was merged as options.
- "DALI status" dashboard rebound to the new names, with the new states. One status box replaces the Summary / Failures pair.

drivers.name: Midi
drivers.description: Advanced MIDI driver — live input/output with any USB or virtual MIDI device, per-channel filtering, pass-through, internal 24-PPQN clock with transport control, Standard MIDI File (SMF) playback and recording, panic/all-notes-off, and a learn helper for mapping physical controls. Streams incoming events as JSON for scripts and dashboards.
drivers.changelog:
# Changelog

## 0.1.2

### Features

- On-demand `Details` documentation layer surfaced to the AI prompt and
  editor hover.

## 0.1.1

Manifest polish — no functional changes.

## 0.1.0

Initial release. Live MIDI input/output over any USB or virtual MIDI
device, per-channel filtering and pass-through, internal 24-PPQN clock
with transport control, Standard MIDI File (SMF) playback and recording,
panic / all-notes-off, and a learn helper for mapping physical controls.
Incoming events stream as JSON for scripts and dashboards.

drivers.name: Signify MultiOne Workflow G2
drivers.description: Signify MultiOne Workflow G2 local REST service (localhost:2023): list interfaces and devices, write feature configurations (AOC, DALI, luminaire data) into Signify LED drivers.
drivers.changelog:
## 0.1.4

- **`online` now updates by itself.** A heartbeat checks `GET /server/v1/status` every `heartbeatMs` (default 5000, 0 = off), skipped while another call runs, so a dashboard shows when Workflow G2 is stopped or started without any button press. New property `serviceMessage` says it in words. Heartbeat calls don't touch `lastResponse` or `lastError`.
- The `multione` template hands the port over with the `dali` connector's `usbRelease` / `usbOpen` (LunatoneLuba 0.4.0 renamed `release` / `open`). **If you use the `multione` connector, update the LunatoneLuba driver to 0.4.0 too.** The "MultiOne G2" dashboard binds `dali.usbConnected`.
